scenarios.title: Import new directory people without disturbing the roster
scenarios.summary: Create real simulated person entries with LDIF, then verify the unchanged roster.
scenarios.objective: Import two new inetOrgPerson entries under ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test. For uid=nova,ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test, supply cn Nova Chen, sn Chen, mail nova@cedar.test and description helpdesk. For uid=theo,ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test, supply cn Theo Moss, sn Moss, mail theo@cedar.test and description helpdesk. Preserve every existing entry and attribute; all requests must succeed in every supplied sample.
steps: Write LDIF, apply it to inspect a sample, then check the resulting directory in every case.
scenarios.explanation: A content record names one new entry with dn and its attributes. inetOrgPerson supplies the person class chain; cn and sn are required, while uid matches this entry's relative name. Repeated attribute lines create multiple values, not multiple people. A blank line starts the next record. Add fails for an existing name, so importing should leave existing people alone.
hints: Read each required field and distinguish a new entry from a change to an existing name.
Use the record result before inspecting state: a failed request cannot be treated as a successful update.
Use content records for the two new people; preserve existing entries.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-09 against LPIC-2v4.5/210.3 and RFC2849/4511/4519/2798. In-memory ASCII LDIF subset; content imports or add/delete/modify, person entries only, mail/description edits, supplied already-established delegated rights. Apply LDIF is a simulator action, not ldapadd/ldapmodify/ldapdelete. No bind, credentials, actual LDAP protocol/server/network, host files, shell execution, controls, rename, passwords, URL loading, complete schema or OpenLDAP ACL configuration. Each test starts with its own sample directory. Utility and server-administration objectives remain unimplemented.

scenarios.title: Repair directory contacts and retire an obsolete entry
scenarios.summary: Choose operations that repair optional contact fields safely across different initial states.
scenarios.objective: For uid=sam,ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test, make mail contain only sam@cedar.test and description contain only on-call. Remove the obsolete leaf entry uid=retired,ou=People,dc=cedar,dc=test. Keep Sam's name, uid and object classes unchanged; preserve every other entry and attribute. Use operations that work when the previous mail list has one value, several values or no value; every request must succeed.
steps: Write LDIF, apply it to inspect a sample, then check the resulting directory in every case.
scenarios.explanation: Modify changes an existing entry. Replace mail establishes the required complete list even if the old attribute was absent; Add appends and leaves aliases behind. Replace description sets the role without depending on an old value. A separate delete record removes only the obsolete leaf. Edits within one Modify are atomic; separate successful records remain if a later request fails.
hints: Read each required field and distinguish a new entry from a change to an existing name.
Use the record result before inspecting state: a failed request cannot be treated as a successful update.
Replace sets a complete attribute list, including when the old attribute is absent. Delete a leaf with its own change record.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-09 against LPIC-2v4.5/210.3 and RFC2849/4511/4519/2798. In-memory ASCII LDIF subset; content imports or add/delete/modify, person entries only, mail/description edits, supplied already-established delegated rights. Apply LDIF is a simulator action, not ldapadd/ldapmodify/ldapdelete. No bind, credentials, actual LDAP protocol/server/network, host files, shell execution, controls, rename, passwords, URL loading, complete schema or OpenLDAP ACL configuration. Each test starts with its own sample directory. Utility and server-administration objectives remain unimplemented.
